mia: I hit a reproducible deadlock where generator streams stall when auth refresh races with request cancellation.
mia: Repro steps: (1) call client.Generator(ctxWithShortTimeout, ...) (2) consume stream slowly (3) token rotation happens mid-stream (4) auth refresh uses request ctx -> refresh aborts, reconnect path stalls, goroutines leak.
mia: Minimal logs captured during flaky run:
```
2026-03-23T14:12:03Z generator: start stream id=st-3a2
2026-03-23T14:12:04Z auth: refresh started token=shortlived
2026-03-23T14:12:05Z generator: write failed err=context canceled
2026-03-23T14:12:10Z generator: no further events, goroutines: 8 (stuck in io.Copy)
```
mia: Simplified anti-pattern inside SDK (we reuse request ctx for background maintenance):
```
func StartStream(ctx context.Context) error {
  // reuse request ctx for auth refresh and long-running generator
  go func() {
    token, err := refreshToken(ctx)
    if err != nil { /* log and return */ }
    _ = token
  }()
  return runGenerator(ctx)
}
```
mia: When app cancels ctx (deadline/user), the refresh goroutine gets canceled too and any retry/reconnect logic that depends on it stalls.
raj: oof. Repro repo? small testcase?
mia: Yes, private repro: https://github.com/redwood/repro-stream-deadlock (will add failing test). Short main excerpt I used to trigger it:
```
func main() {
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
  defer cancel()
  stream, err := client.Generator(ctx, opts)
  if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
  for msg := range stream.Chan() {
    time.Sleep(800 * time.Millisecond)
    fmt.Println(msg)
  }
}
```
tomas: This is classic ctx bleed. Rules we should follow in SDK: (1) Use request ctx only for initial handshake and immediate request-scoped ops; (2) spawn a stream-owned context (streamCtx := context.WithCancel(context.Background())) for background maintenance; (3) use transient ctxs with timeouts for refresh calls so they don't inherit arbitrary request deadlines.
tomas: Example pattern to adopt inside SDK:
```
handshakeCtx := ctx // use for initial dial/handshake only
streamCtx, streamCancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
// background refresher
go func() {
  for {
    select {
    case <-streamCtx.Done():
      return
    case <-time.After(refreshInterval):
      rctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
      _ = refreshAuth(rctx)
      cancel()
    }
  }
}()
// wire streamCancel to stream.Close() so caller controls lifetime
```

raj: Also guard reconnections with a single mutex/connector goroutine so we don't get concurrent reconnect attempts that race on shared state. Add tests that fake a slow refreshToken to ensure we don't leak.
mia: UX wrinkle: apps expect stream to stop quickly when their ctx cancels. If SDK uses stream-owned ctx, we should proactively Close the stream when request ctx is done but still avoid tying long retry loops to request ctx deadlines. Idea: call stream.Close() on request ctx cancellation; background refresh should use transient ctxs so they exit promptly but not be forcibly blocked by the request ctx.
tomas: Agreed. Two pragmatic goals: make stream lifecycle explicit (Close/Err), and keep background maintenance cancellable without being brittle due to caller timeouts.
mia: API proposal: `stream, err := client.GeneratorStream(ctx, opts)` returning an object implementing `Close() error`, `Err() error`, and `Chan() <-chan Message`. SDK should call stream.Close() when initial ctx is canceled to match user expectations.
raj: Let's add a tokenSource abstraction in the SDK so refresh is centralized and unit-testable. We can inject a fake tokenSource in tests that simulates a slow rotation and assert no goroutine leak.
devex-bot: FYI @tomas @raj there's an existing issue template for generator ergonomics: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/issues/6752 (please attach repro). :information_source:
ci-bot: integration (repro-stream-deadlock) Failed: TestStreamCancellation flaked; goroutine dump attached.
mia: I'll open the GH issue with repro, failing test, and goroutine dump. I'll add a small sample app demonstrating the correct streamCtx + transient refresh pattern.
tomas: I can draft a PR that switches the SDK internals to stream-owned contexts and adds unit/integration tests for cancellation/leak scenarios.
mia: Please do. I'll link the repro and tag you in the issue.
raj: Also update quickstart/docs to clarify that the context passed into Generate is handshake-scoped and not for long-running background tasks. Could save users a lot of confusion.
mia: Will add a short blurb in docs once PR merges. Thanks everyone :heart:
